name: Sanctification

objectives.text: Identify that God makes His people holy and helps them grow to be more like Jesus
Name the Holy Spirit as the one who helps God's people grow in holiness
Explain that holy means set apart for God and that God calls His people to be holy because He is holy
List the fruit of the Spirit and give an everyday example of each one
Recite the Westminster Shorter Catechism definition of sanctification and explain its key phrases in your own words
Explain why the Reformed tradition teaches that growth in holiness continues throughout life and is not completed in this life
Explain what Scripture means by dying to sin and living to righteousness
Explain why the Reformed tradition teaches that believers do good works as the fruit of faith and gratitude rather than to earn salvation
Compare justification as a once-for-all act of God with sanctification as an ongoing work of God
Apply the command to put off the old self and put on the new self to concrete situations in school and family life
Explain how God's working and the believer's working relate in sanctification using Philippians 2:12-13
Explain how the Reformed tradition understands God's moral law as a rule of life that guides believers in holy living
Distinguish definitive sanctification as a decisive break with sin's dominion from progressive sanctification as lifelong growth
Describe how sanctification extends to the whole person including mind, will, affections, and body
Analyze Romans 7 and Galatians 5 to describe the ongoing conflict between the Spirit and the flesh in the believer
Explain how Romans 6 grounds sanctification in the believer's sharing in Christ's death and resurrection
Explain how the Word, prayer, sacraments, and fellowship serve as ordinary means God uses in sanctification
Construct a biblical account of the mortification of sin that identifies the Spirit's power and the practical means Scripture commands
Explain why the Reformed tradition teaches that believers' good works remain imperfect yet are accepted by God through Christ
Evaluate perfectionism and antinomianism as opposite errors in light of Scripture and the Reformed confessions
Defend from Scripture the necessity of holiness in the Christian life
Compare the Reformed distinction between justification and sanctification with the Roman Catholic view of justification as infused righteousness
Synthesize the biblical teaching on sanctification into an account of growth toward conformity to the image of Christ

changes: Kept and reworded the real competencies (God makes His people holy, Spirit as helper, lifelong growth, WSC Q35 summary, dying to sin, justification vs sanctification, put off/put on, definitive vs progressive, Spirit vs flesh, Romans 6 basis, means of grace, mortification, perfectionism vs antinomianism, necessity of holiness, image of Christ). Replaced the vague grade 2 'turn away from sin' (overlaps Conversion) with the meaning of holiness, and recast 'observe' as an assessable explanation. Added fruit of the Spirit, good works as gratitude, imperfect good works accepted in Christ, God's working and ours in Philippians 2, the law as rule of life, sanctification of the whole person, and a comparison with the Roman Catholic view. Corrected confession citations to full document names and added WSC Q33, Q88, WLC Q77, WCF 11, 16, 19.6, and Heidelberg Q62 and Q86 where they state the doctrine.
